subject: why are there multiple values for the precision parameter in my CAR model?

messages.author: 7629d0fd6ac72be9
messages.subject: why are there multiple values for the precision parameter in my CAR model?
parts:
Hello,
I am running a CAR model to predict density of spawning redds. I don't understand why the output lists 5 different parameters for region.struct?

Thanks for any help,
Christy

c("inla(formula = formula3, family = \"zeroinflated.nbinomial.1\", ",  "    data = habitat2, verbose = FALSE, control.compute = list(dic = 1, ",  "        mlik = 1, cpo = TRUE), control.predictor = list(compute = T))" )
 hyperparameters:
                                                         mean      sd        0.025quant 0.5quant  0.975quant
size for nbinomial zero-inflated observations            1.279e+00 3.144e-01 7.705e-01  1.242e+00 1.998e+00
zero-probability parameter for zero-inflated nbinomial_1 6.433e-02 3.424e-02 1.750e-02  5.753e-02 1.501e-01
Precision for region.struct                              1.894e+04 1.855e+04 1.291e+03  1.350e+04 6.782e+04

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] why are there multiple values for the precision parameter in my CAR model?
parts:
On 05/01/13 22:43, skinn...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hello,
> I am running a CAR model to predict density of spawning redds. I don't
> understand why the output lists 5 different parameters for region.struct?

The five values are the mean, standard deviation and 0.025,0.5, and
0.975 quantiles of the posterior distribution for the single "Precision"
parameter of the "region.struct" part of your model.
For the precise interpretation of that parameter you'll have to look at
the documentation for the model you are using, for example on
http://www.r-inla.org/models/latent-models

/Finn

Hi,

the model has three hyper-parameters

- size for nbinomial zero-inflated observations
- zero-probability parameter for zero-inflated nbinomial_1
- Precision for region.struct


the first two are the parameters for the likelihood, whereas the last
one is for the 'car' model.
